subject: Transportation Systems
title: Flags of Convenience
description: A micro-lesson that makes Flags of Convenience usable.

hook.text: Most of the world's largest ships fly flags of Panama, Liberia, or the Marshall Islands. Why?

buildup.text: Flags of convenience offer lower taxes, cheaper registration, and less strict labor regulations.

discovery.text: Ship owners register wherever rules are lightest. The crew, cargo, and owner may have no link to the flag.

twist.text: Critics say lax flag states allow unsafe ships and exploited crews. Supporters say it enables global trade.

climax.text: Port state inspections now check foreign-flagged vessels, partially offsetting weak flag-state oversight.

punchline.text: A ship's flag often says more about taxes than nationality.

quiz.question: Why do many ships fly flags of convenience?
options: Lower taxes and less strict regulations
